home.heading: whoami
bio: Brittain Homelab: a four-node Proxmox VE cluster running about twenty services, including file storage, identity, security monitoring, metrics and alerting, backups, and a few fun projects.
Designed, built and operated by John Brittain as a hands-on platform for systems, networking and storage engineering.
Self-hosted infrastructure, Proxmox, VMware vSphere, NetApp ONTAP, ZFS and observability.

network.intro: pfSense firewall with 802.1Q VLANs, a MikroTik 2.5 GbE / 10G core switch, and Pi-hole for DNS. Every guest attaches to one bridge on the main LAN. A dedicated, isolated VLAN carries the nested VMware lab off the GPU node, kept separate from production traffic. Addresses are intentionally left out of this public site.

dns.title: DNS and DHCP
points: A synced Pi-hole pair (primary and backup) provides network-wide DNS filtering
Most guests resolve through Pi-hole; its metrics are scraped by Prometheus
FreeIPA provides LDAP, Kerberos, DNS and a CA for the lab
DHCP runs on pfSense (Kea) for clients; every server uses static addressing

vpn.title: Remote access and exposure
points: Remote access runs through a Tailscale subnet router in its own container, with no inbound ports opened for it
A small set of static port forwards: Plex remote access and game-server ports, with geoblocking scoped to the game ports
Management and internal services are not exposed to the internet

projects.intro: Selected work on the lab, written as problem, approach and result. Headline project first, then the core infrastructure work and a few smaller builds.

items.title: Nested VMware vSphere + NetApp ONTAP lab
summary: Problem: enterprise virtualization and storage skills need real vSphere and ONTAP clusters to practice on, without buying dedicated hardware.

Approach: upgrading the GPU node from 32 GB to 64 GB DDR4 made room for the nested lab. The lab sits on a dedicated, isolated VLAN so nested traffic stays off the production LAN. Three ESXi 8 hosts run nested inside the Proxmox cluster, joined into a vCenter 8.0.2 cluster with shared NFS storage. The cluster hosts a Windows Server 2025 domain controller, a Postgres VM and two Linux test VMs. A two-node NetApp ONTAP 9.19.1 simulator cluster is being built on the nested hosts.
Result: a working vSphere cluster with shared storage and real workloads; the ONTAP cluster is in progress.

items.title: Network upgrades
summary: Problem: storage and gaming traffic was limited to 1 GbE, the real network layout was undocumented, and address assignment and filtering had grown ad hoc.

Approach: upgraded a storage node from 1 GbE to 2.5 GbE with a PCIe RTL8125 card, staging the config with timers that auto-revert if the node loses the router. Found the GPU node's 2.5 GbE card negotiating only 1 Gb/s and moved it to a 2.5 GbE port. Mapped every port on the managed MikroTik switch, moved all servers to static addressing, narrowed geoblocking to the game-server ports only, and added a Wi-Fi 7 access point. Kept a regenerable topology diagram from that data.
Result: both 2.5 GbE nodes link at 2500 Mb/s with cluster quorum verified, a fully documented switch, predictable server addressing and a regenerable diagram.

items.title: Monitoring and alerting
summary: Problem: four nodes, 20 guests and several single-disk USB pools meant a hot CPU, a filling pool or a dying drive could go unnoticed.

Approach: a Docker Compose stack in an LXC container with Prometheus, Grafana and Alertmanager, node_exporter on all four nodes, plus Proxmox and Pi-hole exporters. The Proxmox exporter uses a read-only PVEAuditor API user. Added drive-health alerting (SMART, bad sectors, NVMe wear, media errors, temperature) and a script that posts a daily health summary to Discord at 8:00, 12:00 and 15:00. Fixed ZFS pools reading 0% used and a SMART collector that never ran on an NVMe-only node.
Result: 19 alert rules, 8 scrape targets, two Grafana dashboards, Discord alerting and three daily summaries.

items.title: Backup and data protection
summary: Problem: guests lived on four hosts with different disk layouts, and the big data pools are single disks with no redundancy.

Approach: a Proxmox Backup Server and one cluster-wide vzdump job (every guest, Sundays 01:00, snapshot mode), opt-in ZFS auto-snapshots (daily ×7 and weekly ×4 on file datasets, hourly ×24 on Nextcloud), and manual snapshots plus config backups before risky changes. Audited what the job really covers, including bind-mounted data being outside vzdump.
Result: backups of every guest back to January 2026, a 14.4 TiB datastore with 1.9 TiB used, and snapshot restore points on all data datasets.

items.title: Remote access with Tailscale
summary: A Tailscale subnet router runs in its own container, so the lab is reachable from anywhere without opening inbound ports.

items.title: Redundant DNS with Pi-hole
summary: Pi-hole now runs as a synced primary and backup pair, so DNS filtering survives the loss of either one.
